description: Two weaknesses, and the difference between them is why one gates and one does not. A broken hash does not gate: hashes have honest non-security jobs, and MD5 is only wrong where collision resistance is what makes the thing work, which the call does not say. A broken cipher has no such second life, because nothing needs encryption for a purpose that does not need encryption, so it gates. The AES-GCM call is silent. The second route takes the caller's value as the SUBJECT of a fixed pattern rather than as the pattern, which is ordinary matching.

expected.note: written into the call, and unlike a weak hash this gates
the caller writes the pattern, not the subject
